intent: Establish the baseline Lithic integration as a fully functional ElizaOS-orchestrated payment service purchasing Pyth price feeds, with every line of state management counted, every failure mode tested via Toxiproxy, and the VirtualCardService interface defined as the contract that Stages two and three must satisfy.
key_points: ElizaOS is the real orchestration layer running on Bun inside the Docker container. Payment logic lives in a separate TypeScript module that ElizaOS invokes as an action plugin. The Dockerfile installs Bun via the official oven/bun base image, not Node.js.

The VirtualCardService interface from AGENTS.md is declared in src/interfaces/virtual-card-service.ts and exported. Stage one does not implement it yet. Stage two and three must provide a class that satisfies issueCard and getCardStatus exactly as specified, with settlementTxId, amountUSD, merchantId as input params and cardNumber, expiryDate, cvv, issuedAt as the return shape.

State management is counted using the strict metric definition: lines inside try/catch blocks with retry logic, if/switch blocks handling connection status, and database operations persisting transient transaction states (pending, retrying, reconciling). The state-manager.ts file is annotated with STATE_MGMT_LINE markers for automated counting.

Toxiproxy is a hard Docker Compose dependency for the test suite. The toxiproxy container sits between the service and the Lithic sandbox API. Three named toxics are configured: dropped-connection (simulates cut mid-update via reset_peer), timeout-before-confirm (adds 90-second latency exceeding the 60-second Lithic client timeout), and reconnect-resync (toggles the proxy down then up to force database reconciliation).

Fiat enters via Lithic financial account funding (pre-funded in sandbox). Fiat exits to the merchant through card network settlement. No currency conversion occurs at any point in Stage one. This is the pure-fiat baseline.

An observability console output logs every transaction with timestamps for initiation, authorization, clearing, and settlement. This produces the legacy latency baseline that Stage two and three compare against.
warnings: ElizaOS requires Bun 1.1+ as its runtime. The Dockerfile must use oven/bun:1 as the base image, not node:20-alpine. This changes the container size and build toolchain for all three stages.
Toxiproxy requires a separate container in docker-compose.yml and the toxiproxy-cli binary inside the test runner container. Tests cannot run without the Toxiproxy container healthy.
The VirtualCardService interface is defined but not implemented in Stage one. Any import of this interface in Stage one test code must use type-only imports to avoid runtime errors.

Lithic sandbox webhook delivery requires an externally reachable URL or a local tunnel. When running behind Toxiproxy, the webhook endpoint URL must route through the proxy to enable the dropped-connection test.

The strict state management line count excludes general error handling (e.g., input validation). Only lines matching the three categories in the AGENTS.md definition are counted. Disagreement on boundary lines must be resolved before Stage two begins.
